section.content: I began my academic journey at Carleton University in Ottawa, receiving a BSc in biochemistry in 2020. I had a fantastic experience at Carleton, meeting many wonderful people. My experience in the biochemistry program gave me the mathematical, scientific, and analytical foundations that continue to benefit me in both my academic and professional careers to this day.
section.content2: Following my biochemistry degree, I pursued a BCS in Computer Science at Carleton, graduating in 2022, using my computer science credits from the biochemistry degree to fast-track my studies. During my time in the computer science program, I developed a passion for software development and problem-solving, which has driven me to continue learning and growing in this field.
section.content3: After graduating from Carleton with a BCS in Computer Science and working for a year, I pursued further studies at the Université de Bordeaux in France, as a recipient of the Graduate Studies in France scholarship from the French government.

Inside the classroom, this included learning about marketing and project management, while outside the classroom, I developed a deeper appreciation for different cultures and ways of life, including an appreciation for Bordelais wine and French cheeses.
section.content5: I have a deep appreciation for all the educators, mentors, and peers who have supported me throughout my time in academia. You have all played a significant role in shaping my path in life, and I am grateful for the knowledge and experiences that I have gained along the way!

section.content: Recently, I have begun to experiment with making YouTube videos, with a focus on historical and cultural content. I use Kdenlive and CapCut as my video editors, which I highly recommend.
section.content2: My most recent video is on the discovery of the structure of DNA.
section.content3: Prior to that, I made a video essay on the life of Alcibiades, an Ancient Athenian statesman.
section.content4: For my MBA program, I wrote two significant papers. The first was a market analysis of the online dating industry, highlighting how the existing dating app business model is adverse to the user, and a proposal for a new entrant into the market.
section.content5: The second paper was detailed analysis of the tariff policy of the Trump administration, as of August 2021, looking at White House statements and press releases and examining the potential economic impacts of the tariffs on both the US and global economies. This included a comparison to three historical instances of tariff implementations or political economic accords, and their economic effects; the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930, the Abominable Tariff of 1828, and the Plaza Accord of 1985.

This experience was invaluable to me, as it provided a fantastic understanding of the interaction between hardware and software; many features of higher level programming languages are the direct result of hardware capabilities.

This was my first exposure to public sector work, at a very interesting time. I reviewed over $10 million in grant applications related to COVID-19, and successfully collated, cleaned, and analyzed rapid antigen testing data from pharmacies and small businesses across Canada.

01-25-2026.title: Europe must concede nothing to the Trump Administration, for its own sake.

content.paragraph1: In January 2026, US President Donald J. Trump announced, on Truth Social, that the United States would be implementing a blanket 10% tariff on all imports from select European countries (Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and Finland), starting February 1st, 2026, in response to Danish refusal to give up sovereignty over Greenland. President Trump has repeatedly stated that American national security is at risk if Greenland is not under US control, and threatened to raise tariffs to 25% if Denmark does not comply.
content.paragraph2: First of all, one must address the sheer ridiculousness of the notion that the United States "needs" Greenland for national security reasons. Thus far, American reasoning for wanting the territory largely falls within two main lines of reasoning: the first, being that there is an imminent threat that China or Russia will use opening Arctic waterways to gain strategic leverage over the United States, and that the US needs a greater military presence in Greenland to counter this threat; the second, is that Greenland is rich in rare earth minerals, which are necessary for the production of modern technology, such as solar panels and military hardware.
content.paragraph3: These claims are dubious at best; the US already has a base on Greenland, and the 1951 Greenland Defense Agreement gives the US wide breadth to expand its presence on the island if it were to so choose.
content.paragraph4: As for rare earth minerals, Greenland does have significant deposits. However, Greenland only ranks 8th worldwide for confirmed deposits of rare earth minerals... behind the United States itself. Exploratory drilling is also merely an estimate of deposits, and does not mean it is economically viable to extract them. Finally, despite their name, rare earth minerals are actually relatively abundant in the Earth's crust; the issue is that they are found in small concentrations in other ores, and require significant processing to extract.
content.paragraph5: However, let us put aside, for the moment, all of that. The notion that the US requires Greenland for "national security" is farcical. I would also be militarily and economically safer if I owned Greenland. I would also be safer if I owned Iceland, and the United States, even the entire planet. But alas, we live in a world of other human beings, and need to learn to share resources like adults.
content.paragraph6: Alas, President Trump has since posted, on January 21st, again on Truth Social, that a "framework of a future deal" had been reached with Mark Rutte, the current Secretary General of NATO. While details remain fuzzy, Trump has stated that:
content.paragraph7: The time limit is infinity, meaning there is no time limit. It's forever. You know, you're about 99 years, 50 years. It's forever. That was discussed. We can do anything we want. We can do military, we can do anything we want, and it's being negotiated. And let's see what happens. I think it'll be good.
content.paragraph8: Implying that Denmark will, in fact, concede some territory to the United States. While this seems like a trivial concession to make a potentially disastrous diplomatic row go away, Europe is making a grave mistake by making any concessions to the Trump administration.
content.paragraph9: By allowing the Americans to threaten and bully their way to any sort of shift in the status quo, particularly one that involves conceding territory, Europe is proving to President Trump and his supporters that such tactics are effective. By choosing to cede even the smallest amount of territory, Trump supporters believe that the President is a master negotiator, a savvy businessman who garners concessions without firing a shot, by choosing to anchor negotiations at an extreme position, and then working backwards to gain a favorable outcome.
content.paragraph10: President Trump, for all his bluster and unpredictability, does respect strength. He has repeatedly expressed respect for President Xi of China and President Putin of Russia, and disrespected pliable leaders such as Rutte (whose mandate is now, admittedly, maintaining NATO, even if it's too the detriment of the majority of its members, including the Netherlands, of which he is a former Prime Minister). By refusing to concede anything to the Trump administration, Europe will be sending a clear message that such tactics will not work, and that the United States must engage in good faith negotiations, rather than trying to bully its way to favorable outcomes.
content.paragraph11: The Greenland Crisis, while still treated as a sideshow in the United States, represents an existential threat to NATO, Canada (whom Trump has already expressed interest in annexing, and would be surrounded on three sides if an American Greenland were to come to pass), and possibly some EU countries themselves. While Europe remains divided, there is hope that facing such a grave threat to their sovereignty will bring urgency for the Europeans to work together, and perhaps, just maybe, federate.
content.paragraph12: Even if this commentary seems politically charged, this is as much game theory as it is geopolitics. The Trump administration's style of negotiation is akin to brinksmanship, and they do it much better than the previous Biden administration.
content.paragraph13: While the hour is dark for the west, we come from a rich heritage of free thinkers, who have adapted and adopted to political systems and ideals when the old ways no longer served us. What the numbers do not show, is a Europe that is stronger and richer than it thinks; with a robust manufacturing base, a strong agricultural sector, innovative tech hubs, capable militaries, and an unmatched cultural heritage. The numbers don't tell the whole story, with a United States that increasingly sells financial services and vaporware that provide an illusion of prosperity where there is less and less to be found. With some encouragement and bravery, it is possible for the rest of the west to come together and find a new path forward, one that does not involve kowtowing to whichever autocrat feels like throwing around their weight that day.

01-30-2026.title: Trump's selection of Kevin Warsh as Chair of the Federal Reserve is a manifestation of corruption within the Trump administration.

content.paragraph1: On January 29th, 2026, US President Donald Trump nominated financier Kevin Warsh to be the next Chair of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, succeeding the highly regarded Jerome Powell, who has recently become the focus of a legal attack from the Trump administration. President Trump has repeatedly expressed frustration with the Federal Reserve Board's refusal to lower the federal funds rate (FFR), which influences the overnight loan rate between financial institutions.
content.paragraph2: On the surface, Warsh appears to be a perfectly acceptable candidate for the job; he previously sat on the Federal Reserve Board from 2006 to 2011, including during the tumultuous Great Recession. He is well educated, holding a BA from Stanford University in public policy, including concentrations in economics and statistics, and has a JD from Harvard Law School, so he is not light on the prestigious credentials that many in American political circles want to see from their fellow public officials. During his time in the private sector, he was a Vice President and Executive Director at Morgan Stanley. Before being nominated as Fed Chair, Warsh was working as a distinguished visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford. The man is not a lightweight in the world of finance and capital markets, to be sure.
content.paragraph3: What is more interesting, however, is Warsh's personal connections. Warsh is married to Jane Lauder, the granddaughter of Estée Lauder, the founder of the eponymous cosmetics company, whom he met at Stanford. While Estée Lauder is publicly traded today, listed on the NYSE under ticker EL, the Lauder family retains a significant financial stake in the company, and Jane herself is an Executive Vice President at the company, running the Origins and Clinique brands. She is also a billionaire in her own right, with Forbes estimating her net worth to be 2.7 billion USD as of April 2025.
content.paragraph4: Jane Lauder is not the political connection herself though; that would be her father, Warsh's father-in-law, Ronald Lauder, who Forbes estimates to have a net worth of 5 billion USD (henceforth, any reference to "Lauder" in this post will refer to Ronald Lauder, not his daughter). Lauder is a Republican megadonor, having donated over 5 million USD to Trump's super PAC, MAGA Inc., in March 2025. He is a major source of pro-Israel funding in American politics, and also takes an active interest in Israeli politics, where he was investigated for gifts to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
content.paragraph5: Lauder is not merely another billionaire, passively throwing around fractions of his net worth on pseudo-bribery in order to garner support for political causes he cares about; he was formerly the US Ambassador to Austria from 1986 to 1987, appointed by President Reagan. He is also a personal friend of President Donald Trump, presumably having met through their business dealings in the New York City metro area, from which they both hail. Both also attended the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School of Business, which Lauder has continued to be involved with, although he reportedly graduated in 1965, one year prior to Trump's transfer to the school from Fordham University.
content.paragraph6: Lauder has been credited not only with influencing the Trump administration's stance on Israel; in a January 2026 article by Tom Burgis for The Guardian, Lauder was also the origin of Trump's idea that the United States should acquire Greenland. Lauder's financial interests on the island include a plan to bottle "luxury" water from an island in Baffin Bay, off Greenland's west coast, and to generate hydroelectric energy to power aluminium smelting, which requires the Hall-Héroult process, a highly energy intensive method of extracting aluminium from bauxite ore.
content.paragraph7: Keep in mind that lobbyists in the US are supposed to be disclosed to the public through the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995, which Lauder is, of course, not registered under, so Lauder's activities fall more into the realm of money-for-access than lobbying. As it is has become more and more expensive to remain competitive in American politics, it is no secret that American elected officials have oft been influenced by the political donors they rely upon to seek and maintain office. However, the potential heading of the Federal Reserve, the nominally independent body that ultimately controls American monetary policy, by a non-impartial actor, is a far greater threat to continued American prosperity and global hegemony than some military forrays into banana republics and remote islands (which were, in and of themselves, major and ill-advised political crises).
content.paragraph8: Mr. Warsh is his own man, and, assuming he is confirmed, it remains to be seen how he uses his office to manage America's monetary policy. By no means does having a politically connected wife and father-in-law mean that Warsh will act in their, or the President's, interests, rather than those of America. Thus far, markets seem to be responding positively to Warsh's nomination, with US 10Y bond yields stabilizing after a brief jump, and precious metals, common "safe haven" assets that had seen a near parabolic rise in January 2026, dropping sharply, with gold down almost 10% and silver down over 25% on January 30th, possibly the largest destructions of paper wealth ever seen in a single day in dollar terms (over 5 trillion USD). In general, markets seem optimistic about Warsh as Trump's nominee, and believe he will be a competent choice for the role.
content.paragraph9: Having said all that, many do not yet seem to realize Warsh's arms-length connection to the Trump White House. The President has already made it abundantly clear that assuming the powers of the Presidency has not put him, or his family, above engaging in a bit of profiteering, with the net worths of Trump's immediate family members skyrocketing since his return to office. Trump's crypto meme coin, $TRUMP, has had a peak market capitalization of 27 billion USD, and Bloomberg reports that Donald and Melania have seen their net worth increase by over 3 billion USD in his first year back in office. Jared Kushner and his wife Ivanka Trump have raised 4.6 billion USD from Gulf investors for their latest business venture, the private equity firm Affinity Partners. Even Trump's youngest son, Barron, has reportedly made over 80 million USD from selling crypto tokens.
content.paragraph10: While it would be comforting to see Warsh act independently of the Trump administration, given Trump's overt attacks on the Federal Reserve and its independence, it is difficult to see the President not attempting to influence Warsh's actions as Fed Chair in some capacity. Any further indications that the Federal Reserve is no longer politically independent would further damage America's standing as the global center of financial markets, and could result in the rest of the planet continuing to seek alternatives to the US dollar. While the President may not fully grasp how the global financial system has worked to support continued American economic hegemony, the consequences of this choice may be dire, and they will soon be felt by everyone's pocketbooks. We can only hope that Mr. Warsh will continue to act with the professionalism and impartiality that has defined his career in the public service thus far.
content.paragraph11: ADDENDUM: Since I first posted this, another batch of files related to the Jeffrey Epstein case have been released, which show that both Warsh and Jane Lauder were guests on Epstein's private island.

03-23-2026.title: How to easily create a cryptocurrency in 2026.

content.paragraph1: This post is a quick guide to deploying a new token on the Ethereum blockchain. As the crypto space continues to prance around the outskirts of mainstream finance, it is important to understand how easily tokens can be deployed on L1 platforms like Ethereum. Please keep in mind that this is not an endorsement of the cryptocurrency space.
content.paragraph2: To begin, install the MetaMask browser wallet at the following URL. MetaMask is a free browser wallet that is broadly accepted in the crypto space, meaning it has a high degree of interoperability with various cryptocurrency tools and applications. Click on the "Get Started" button to install the extension and create a wallet.
content.paragraph3: Once you have installed and setup your wallet, navigate to the settings menu and ensure that the "Show test networks" option is enabled. Use the dropdown menu to select the Sepolia testnet. This will allow us to deploy our token on a test network before going live on the Ethereum mainnet, which will cost Ether.
content.paragraph4: Now, navigate to the following URL to receive free Sepolia testnet Ether. Enter your wallet address (which can be found at the top of your MetaMask wallet extension) and click the "Get 0.05 Sepolia ETH" button. While it doesn't have any cash value, this testnet Ether is required to pay for deploying our token contract on the Sepolia testnet.
content.paragraph5: We will be using an open source library of smart contracts called OpenZeppelin to create our token. OpenZeppelin provides implementations of basic Ethereum tokens, according to standards set out by the Ethereum Foundation. Programming on the Ethereum blockchain is done in Solidity, a Java-esque bracketed language. Navigate to the following URL to open the "Contracts Wizard" tool.
content.paragraph6: Select the ERC20 token standard, and provide a name, ticker symbol, and a number of tokens to premint (preferably a large number, so as to give a sufficient supply for testing and liquidity). The Solidity code will update automatically to reflect your entered values. Now, select the "Open in Remix" button at the top right of the code editing window. This will open the Remix IDE, a web-based IDE for deploying code to the Ethereum blockchain.
content.paragraph7: On the left side of Remix, find the "Solidity compiler" tab and click the "Compile" button. Ensure that you are compiling the main Solidity file associated with your token (the one you saw in OpenZeppelin), and not one of the imported library files.
content.paragraph8: Once the code is successfully compiled, navigate to the "Deploy & run transactions" tab. Ensure that the "Environment" dropdown is set to "Browser Extension > Sepolia Testnet - MetaMask", which will allow Remix to connect to your MetaMask wallet, as well as specify to deploy on the Sepolia testnet. The "Account" dropdown should automatically populate with your wallet address. Click the "Deploy & Verify" button - MetaMask should open automatically and prompt you to confirm the transaction.
content.paragraph9: Congratulations! After a few minutes (depending on the level of activity on the Sepolia testnet), your token will be deployed! You can see a time estimate for completion of the transaction in MetaMask, however it is usually less than 30 seconds. To deploy on the mainnet, simply switch the "Environment" dropdown to "Browser Extension > Injected Provider - MetaMask", and ensure that you have enough mainnet Ether in your wallet to pay for the transaction.
content.paragraph10: Once the transaction is complete, copy the token address at the bottom left of the Remix IDE, under the "Deployed Contracts" section. This address is the transaction hash that stores your deployed contract on the Ethereum blockchain.
content.paragraph11: Now, we will import your new token to your wallet to see the tokens. Open your MetaMask wallet, click the three dots to the right of the network dropdown and select "Import tokens". Ensure you are still on the Sepolia testnet, paste the token address into the "Token Contract Address" field, and the rest of the fields should populate automatically. Follow the prompts to finish importing the token.
content.paragraph12: Again, a final congratulations! You have successfully created and deployed your own cryptocurrency token on the Ethereum blockchain! This token is fully functional and can be transacted with friends or colleagues. If you would like further details, or cryptocurrency consultation in general, you know where to find me.

06-28-2026.title: The revocation of citizenship is hypocritical and undermines the concept of being a citizen.

content.paragraph1: In the past decade, a wave of conservative populism has swept western politics. Part of this conservative moral panic includes a concern about the mass migration of "others" entering western countries, where they will undermine the social fabric, act with impunity, mooch off social welfare programs, and destroy the conhesive sense of identity that nation-states rely upon to continue their existence. There is much to be said on this topic, and there is merit to the idea that a cohesive sense of identity is important to having a productive society. Immigrants, particularly naturalized citizens, need, to some degree, to desire to contribute to a society, in order for that society to continue to prosper, and for their own choice to immigrate to remain sensible. Great societies are built by a populace working to make them great, not by a populace looking to extract the maximum value from the collective.
content.paragraph2: However, the aforementioned panic, that foreign people are coming to western countries to extract wealth, knowledge and resources for their own benefit, has recently given rise to a troubling phenomenon; countries attempting to restrict or revoke citizenship, sometimes in violation of their own laws and constitutions. The most glaring example of this is in the US, where the Trump administration has recently moved to revoke the naturalized citizenship of 17 Americans, most of whom were accused of serious crimes, including sexual abuse of a minor, and a $36 million healthcare fraud.
content.paragraph3: Make no mistake; these individuals are very deserving of punishment under the law, and the US' Immigration and Nationality Act does allow for denaturalization of a citizen if fraud occurred during the naturalization process. Nothing in this essay is to argue that these individuals are innocent, or I doubt anyone will care if they are denaturalized. However, we have a path for punishing citizens, called the criminal justice system. Moreover, citizenship is one of the few legal dividing lines we have, to guarantee certain rights, such as freedom of movement. In practice, while non-citizens technically have a right to due process, the power of the state to deport non-citizens (even ones with legal status), has increasingly deprived them of that right. Removing these people's citizenship not only does collective damage, but is a serious attempt to deprive Americans of legal protections.
content.paragraph4: In Italy, the Deputy Prime Minister, Matteo Salvini, has uttered the non-sensical phrase "Citizenship cannot be for life." He continued, "As far as I am concerned, both the residence permit and citizenship are an act of trust from the Italian people, who give respect and demand respect in return. It is not a lifetime contract." While on the surface, citizens may be pleased to hear a public official threatening serious consequences for crime, for a public official to say such things, is to completely destroy the meaning of these legal statuses. Revoking citizenships, even with good reasons, transforms them from a known quantity, a category with rights and responsibilities, to a fun freebie, to be arbitrarily granted and taken away, depending on who is in power.
content.paragraph5: In Canada, the federal government has recently been sending letters to citizens naturalized by a new citizenship-by-descent law, telling them that their citizenship has been "suspended", due to undisclosed information. This has occurred after citizenship certificates have been issued and ceremonies held. The Canadian government must learn the hard way that the time to do due diligence for citizenship application is before approval, not after.
content.paragraph6: Opening the door to revoking citizenship after it has been granted completely nullifies the entire concept of citizenship, and the protections it offers. Those revoking the citizenships are also citizens, conceptually on the same footing as those they condemn - revoking, or attempting to suspend or revoke citizenship, after it has been granted, creates an obscure two-tiered system, where some citizens are implicitly more legitimate than others. It is not for one citizen to judge another citizen to be an outsider, undeserving of the status that has already been accorded to them.
content.paragraph7: Not every person who comes to a western country should automatically receive citizenship. As prices rise and the global south develops, it is increasingly non-sensical for western countries to import mass amounts of human capital; it does not benefit the recipient countries as much as in the past, nor the migrants themselves. However, it remains simultaneously illogical to begin stripping citizenship after it has been accorded. To do so reduces citizenship to a meaningless piece of paper, one that can be arbitrarily given and revoked depending on who is in power. The time to do due diligence on a new citizen is before the citizen ceremony and paperwork has been finalized, not after. Afterwards, they should be subject to the same judicial procedures as any other citizen. To do otherwise only serves to cheapen citizenship for us all.

08-27-2026.title: Did Rosalind Franklin discover the structure of DNA?

content.paragraph1: The discovery of the structure of DNA, or deoxyribonucleic acid, remains one of the landmark scientific achievements of the 20th century. In April 1953, in an issue of the scientific journal Nature, James Watson and Francis Crick, researchers at the Cavendish Lab at Cambridge University, published a short paper, less than a page long, proposing a molecular structure for DNA, which consisted of two intertwined helices, most commonly known as the double helix. While it would take further scientific investigation to confirm this structure, today, there is broad scientific consensus that the 1953 structure proposed by Watson and Crick is correct. In 1962, James Watson, Francis Crick and Maurice Wilkins, a colleague at King's College, were jointly awarded the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine, for "their discoveries concerning the molecular structure of nucleic acids and its significance for information transfer in living material."
content.paragraph2: Humans have implicitly understood the concept of genetics and heritable traits for thousands of years. Over 9000 years ago, Mesoamerican groups were selectively breeding corn. In the old world, cruciferous vegetables of the Brassica genus were selectively bred to yield different vegetables, such as broccoli, kale and Brussels sprouts. Between 1856 and 1863, the Augustinian, Austrian monk Gregor Mendel bred pea plants, demonstrating the concept of "simple inheritance", where two plants with different versions of the same gene, called alleles, can pass down different versions to their offspring, giving rise to distinct physical variations, called phenotypes. And, of course, in 1859, the famous biologist Charles Darwin would publish his landmark text, On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, in which he proposes the theory of evolution.
content.paragraph3: While these discoveries demonstrated an understanding that creatures inherited physical traits from their ancestors, it was only in the late 19th century that we began to understand the biochemical mechanisms by which this occurs. In 1869, Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher isolated the DNA molecule, and in the early 20th century, biochemist Phoebus Levene identified the key chemical components of DNA. The molecule contained four different bases, called nucleotides. These are:
content.paragraph4: These four bases work together to transmit information. The molecule also contains a sugar-phosphate backbone. In DNA, the guanine pairs with cytosine, and the adenine pairs with thymine. In the 1940s, Erwin Chargaff proved that these pairings were not in equal amounts, with the amounts of adenine matching the amount of thymine, and the amount of guanine equalling the amount of cytosine. In 1952, Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase, working at the Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, demonstrated that viruses transmitted their genetic information using DNA, which provided important clues towards proving that DNA was, in fact, the encoding mechanism used to pass down genes from parents to offspring.
content.paragraph5: By the 1950s, we knew the chemical composition of DNA, but not the structure of the molecule. Understanding the molecular structure of DNA is key to understanding how our cells use its information to create the proteins that help shape our physiology. By this point, the question of the structure of DNA was highly topical in the scientific community, with high-profile scientists proposing their own models for the structure of DNA. Linus Pauling, a biochemist who would go on to win the Nobel Prize twice and develop the concept of electronegativity, proposed a three-stranded structure of DNA in early 1953, with the purines and pyrimidine bases on the outside, two months before Watson and Crick would publish their landmark paper. Pauling's model was quickly disproven, but its publication created a sense of urgency at Cambridge to be the first to propose the correct model. Watson and Crick's resulting paper would go on to be highly impactful, and is a seminal paper in the field of molecular biology.
content.paragraph6: Before continuing, we should briefly introduce our "main characters": James Watson was an American researcher in his mid-20s at the time of the discovery. He completed his undergraduate degree at the University of Chicago in Zoology in 1947, and completed his PhD in microbiology at Indiana University Bloomington in 1950, at the age of 22. His doctorate was supervised by Italian biochemist Salvador Luria, who would win the Nobel Prize himself in 1969, and is the namesake of Luria Broth, a medium used to grow bacteria in the lab. Originally interested in ornithology, Watson was highly ambitious, and seeing the rapid pace of microbiology research at the time, sought out Luria to be his PhD supervisor. After his graduation, he spent a year as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Copenhagen under another noteworthy biochemist, Herman Kalckar, although their research interests quickly diverged. He arrived at Cambridge in September 1951, and heard Maurice Wilkins give a talk on the applications of x-ray crystallography on DNA, reinforcing his interest in the applications of the technology.
content.paragraph7: Francis Crick was a Brit from Northampton, who had originally begun his scientific career as a physicist at University College London, doing a PhD researching the viscosity of water at high temperatures, which would be abandoned when his laboratory was destroyed during the Second World War. He spent the remainder of the conflict doing research for the Admiralty, the department of the British government that commands the Royal Navy. By 1947, Crick had resumed his academic career, this time at Cambridge, and shifted his interests towards the biological sciences, as he too had witnessed the rapid pace of advancement in the field at the time. Initially, Crick worked on researching the physical properties of cytoplasm, before moving to the Cavendish Lab, where he would discover the structure of DNA. He would receive his PhD from Cambridge in 1954.
content.paragraph8: In recent years, as the presence and awareness of the impact of female researchers on science has grown, you will often see comments online, alleging that James Watson and Francis Crick "stole" the discovery of the structure of DNA from a colleague, Rosalind Franklin. Franklin was a chemist who had received her PhD from Cambridge in 1945. By 1951, she was working at King's College London on a fellowship, and was a subject matter expert in the field of x-ray crystallography, an imaging technique that offers clues to the atomic structure of molecules. When x-rays pass through a target molecule, they pass through the cloud of electrons that surrounds the nucleus, showing the bonds between the atoms. Clever and experienced scientists can use high quality x-ray diffraction images to make inferences about the atomic structure of a molecule.
content.paragraph9: Franklin was originally supposed to work with proteins and lipids at King's College, but was reassigned by the lab director, John Randall, to work with Maurice Wilkins, who was leading a research group investigating the structure of DNA, and assigned her a PhD student, Raymond Gosling. Gosling himself would go on to receive his PhD from King's College in 1954. This reassignment immediately caused friction in the research group; Wilkins was soft-spoken and timid, whereas Franklin was brash and opinionated, and the two immediately developed a mutual dislike. Although literature sometimes states that Wilkins was Franklin's superior, this is a misunderstanding, intentionally disseminated by James Watson, who refers to Franklin as a "research assistant" in his book. In actuality, Wilkins and Franklin were to be co-researchers in the group.
content.paragraph10: Before proceeding, we should also discuss the physical locations in this story. Watson and Crick were researchers at the Cavendish Laboratory at Cambridge, and were largely focused on theoretical model building. Franklin, Wilkins and Gosling were performing their research at King's College in London. Franklin had a far more rigorous, modern approach to scientific research, with a heavy emphasis on experimental data. Both groups were in regular contact with each other and fraternised, with Wilkins being a personal friend of Crick's.
content.paragraph11: In her first year in the lab, Franklin noted "Evidence for spiral structure. Straight chain untwisted is highly improbable. Absence of reflections on meridian in crystalline form suggests spiral structure" in her research notes, although the helical structure of DNA was already popular in the scientific community, having been first proposed by Danish researcher Sven Furberg. She and Gosling also established that there were two different isomers of DNA; that is, two different structural configurations, of the DNA molecule, A-DNA, which they referred to as "crystalline", and B-DNA, which they termed "wet." In November 1951, Franklin presented these findings to colleagues at King's College, suggesting that DNA was either a double or triple helix. Due to the growing divide in the lab and animosity between Wilkins and Franklin, Randall assigned Wilkins to work on B-DNA and Franklin to work on A-DNA. At this time, Watson and Crick were building theoretical models based on ongoing research output from various labs in Europe and North America.
content.paragraph12: For a moment, let us take a step back and think about what these scientists are attempting to achieve here. Humans have never seen molecules, let alone atoms, with the naked eye. We can only make inferences about their nature and structure from their behaviour and observation using sophisticated scientific instruments. In this instance, these scientists are attempting to assemble a jigsaw puzzle, with numerous changing parts, where they don't know what the "correct" solution looks like, using shadows from x-rays. This would be a significant scientific challenge, even with modern equipment.
content.paragraph13: By 1952, Franklin was no longer convinced that A-DNA was helical in nature. She and Gosling wrote a fake obituary for helical A-DNA, to poke fun at Wilkins, who still believed that both forms of DNA were helical (he ended up being correct).
content.paragraph14: At this time, Franklin and Gosling were aggressively collecting more experimental data. In May 1952, Gosling took the famous "photo 51" that would be used as a crucial piece of evidence to support Watson and Crick's model. Producing x-ray crystallographic images takes a prolonged period of time; after identifying the A and B isomers of DNA, Franklin realised that humidity fluctuations were causing the DNA molecule to shift between isomers during the imaging process, which could take over two days. Franklin and Gosling built a specialised experimental apparatus, strictly controlling the humidity of the environment over 62 hours while the image was produced, creating exceptionally clear pictures. Photo 51, the 51st image they produced, was set aside, as it was of the B form of DNA, which Franklin was not focusing on, as per her deal with Wilkins.
content.paragraph15: In February 1953, a team from Cambridge, including Max Perutz, Crick's PhD supervisor, visited King's College to review their research, as part of the Medical Research Council's biennial report. Perutz returned and shared the report with Crick, which included crucial data about DNA compiled by Franklin, including unit-cell measurements, which could be used to deduce interatomic distances. Much debate has occurred about whether Perutz should have shared this report.
content.paragraph16: By 1953, Franklin was fed up with the toxic work environment at King's College, and committed to leave for Birkbeck College, now part of the University of London. Gosling was reassigned to Wilkins as his new supervisor, and he dutifully handed over his and Franklin's research notes and photos to Wilkins. Around this time, James Watson visited King's College and spoke with Wilkins. After some discussion, Wilkins pulled out the now famous photo 51 from a drawer and showed it to Watson. In his book, Watson describes the moment Wilkins showed him photo 51:
content.paragraph17: Watson immediately understood the importance of photo 51. Crick had previously published a paper in Acta Crystallographica, describing the theoretical crystallography of a helix. Watson also immediately recognised the dark areas at the top and bottom of the photo as the sugar phosphate backbone of two distinct strands.
content.paragraph18: Upon returning to Cambridge, Watson and Crick set to work on building a model out of metal plates and wires, but found they were still confused about the precise nature of the base pairing on the interior of the double helix. Watson was still convinced that the bases on the inside followed a "like-with-like" pairing, but the position of the hydrogen atoms on the bases made it impossible to form the hydrogen bonds that keep both helices together. The final piece of the puzzle came when a colleague, chemist Jerry Donohue, visiting from the USA on a six-month fellowship, suggested that the bases were likely in the keto form, changing the locations of the hydrogens on the molecule. Playing around with the model, Watson and Crick realised that the base pairings were adenine-thymine and guanine-cytosine, and that the strands were facing in opposite directions, referred to as "antiparallel". Such a model aligned perfectly with the previously discovered Chargaff's rule.
content.paragraph19: With these final realisations, the A-T/C-G base pairing and the antiparallel strands, Watson and Crick were able to assemble their final model. Crick famously went across a street to The Eagle Pub in Cambridge, proclaiming that they had "discovered the secret of life".
content.paragraph20: The model built by Watson and Crick at the Cavendish lab set out a few basic principles that, mostly, still stand today:
content.paragraph21: In the initial paper published in Nature announcing their model, Watson and Crick acknowledge Donohue, Wilkins, Franklin, and their coworkers at King's College, writing:
content.paragraph22: Reportedly, Wilkins had been offered co-authorship, but declined. In the same issue, Franklin and Gosling published a paper entitled "Molecular Configuration in Sodium Thymonucleate", sodium thymonucleate being a historical name for the sodium salt of DNA. In the paper, Franklin and Gosling describe their experimental setup and methods for imaging DNA retrieved from calves, and discuss their evidence that DNA is helical, that the phosphate groups are in the outer sugar-phosphate backbone, and that the molecule has a diameter of 20 Angstroms. Wilkins, Stokes, and another colleague, Herbert Wilson, published a paper in the same issue, titled "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: Molecular Structure of Deoxypentose Nucleic Acids". While all three papers dealt with aspects of the crystallography and molecular structure of DNA, ultimately, Watson and Crick have taken the bulk of the credit for the discovery.
content.paragraph23: Between her leaving King's College and her death, Franklin worked on structures of the tobacco mosaic and polio viruses with colleagues J.D. Bernal and Aaron Klug. Klug would also go on to win the Nobel Prize in 1982, and would publicly advocate for the recognition of Franklin's work on the structure of DNA, using her research notes to argue that she was closer to discovering the structure of DNA than Watson claimed. Reportedly, Franklin remained on good terms with Francis Crick and his wife, who visited her and exchanged correspondence during her final illness.
content.paragraph24: Watson returned to the United States in 1956 and worked for the biology department at Harvard University, before becoming the Director of Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory. He would leave in 2007, after making controversial statements about a link between race and intelligence. Watson died in 2025.
content.paragraph25: Crick received his PhD in 1954 and continued research in the field of molecular biology, helping to discover the mechanisms by which organisms use the information encoded by DNA to manufacture proteins. In 1957, he coined the term "central dogma" of molecular biology, referring to how DNA is used to produce RNA, which is translated into proteins. In the 1970s, he became a Distinguished Research Professor at the Salk Institute for Biological Sciences in California. He died in San Diego in 2004.
content.paragraph26: In 1962, Watson, Crick and Wilkins shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery. Neither Franklin nor Gosling was mentioned in the Nobel citation. Franklin had died in 1958 of ovarian cancer, possibly due to her years of exposure to radiation from her research, although ovarian cancer is disproportionately common in people of Ashkenazi Jewish heritage. While the Nobel Institute only explicitly updated their statutes to exclude dead awardees in 1974, a longstanding unwritten rule held that Nobel laureates should be living.
content.paragraph27: In 1968, Watson would publish a memoir titled "The Double Helix", a first-hand account of the discovery of DNA, which recounted his version of the events surrounding the discovery of the structure of DNA. The book was immediately controversial, and evoked public responses from a number of the researchers involved. In it, Watson is not outright hostile to Franklin, but refers to her as "Rosy" (a nickname she hated) and portrays her as a hot-headed lab assistant, and describes intentionally antagonising her. This book, as well as other comments Watson made in interviews, specifically regarding scientific racism, brought much controversy, although he would remain a high-profile scientist until his death. The book is commonly viewed as being unfair to Franklin, and failing to adequately recognise her contributions to the discovery.
content.paragraph28: Maurice Wilkins wrote his own autobiography in 2003, shortly before his death. Titled "The Third Man of the Double Helix: The Autobiography of Maurice Wilkins", it has also been criticised for giving insufficient credit to Stokes, Wilson, and other colleagues, though the book was not as widely read as The Double Helix.
content.paragraph29: Many today argue about whether or not the discovery of DNA was "stolen" from Franklin. While her work was crucial to the eventual paper that is credited with the discovery, the truth is very nuanced, and "stolen" is not an accurate term. A more accurate claim would be that Watson and Crick used Franklin's data without crediting her, a contribution that would at least merit her getting her name on the paper today, although there are arguably several individuals who also deserved this honour, including Gosling and Wilkins, one of the few members of the research groups who was a biochemist and focused on the molecular structure of DNA from the very beginning. A few key factors that undermine the claim that the discovery was stolen include:
content.paragraph30: What is true, however, is that Franklin's work and role in the discovery were downplayed, both by James Watson and other colleagues, as well as much of the mainstream scientific community and media, due to rampant sexism at the time. Watson used his book to portray Franklin as an angry lab assistant who was incapable of drawing her own conclusions, whilst using her data and evidence to inform his own research. Franklin was a leading expert in x-ray crystallography, and she and Gosling spent a large amount of time fine-tuning the crystallographic process to image DNA, which resulted in photo 51, which caused Watson to have his "eureka" moment about the precise structure of the molecule.
content.paragraph31: It is worth noting that both the Cavendish lab and King's College had other high-profile female researchers, who had more positive relationships with the male researchers, so it is possible that personal animosity played a factor. One of the first colleagues to see the completed model of DNA was Dorothy Hodgkin, who would go on to win a Nobel Prize herself for the discovery of the structure of vitamin B12.
content.paragraph32: Today, a plaque at King's College recognises five key researchers for their role in the discovery of the structure of DNA:
content.paragraph33: Watson and Crick obviously deserve recognition for the discovery, as do Donohue and other colleagues.
content.paragraph34: However, to credit any one person, or argue that the discovery was "stolen", is folly. Scientific discovery is the result of humanity's drive for knowledge, and the compounding work of numerous dedicated researchers. As Newton said, "If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants."
principles: DNA is a double helix, two intertwined strands with bases on the inside. Adenine creates hydrogen bonds with thymine, and cytosine with guanine, holding the two strands together through hydrogen bonding and allowing for other molecules to interact with the DNA.

The sugar-phosphate backbones are antiparallel, i.e. running in opposite directions. In organic chemistry, the carbon atoms in a molecule are numbered according to set rules. If you were to cut the DNA molecule at a pair of nucleotides, then one strand would terminate at the 5' carbon, and the other at the 3' carbon.

The model built by Watson and Crick was right-handed. That is, if you point your right thumb along the axis of the double helix towards the 3' end, the direction you would curl your fingers is the direction of the helix. Scientists have since discovered a left-handed version of the molecule, Z-DNA, but this was not known at the time.
factors: Ultimately, the final model was assembled by Watson and Crick, which included crucial details, such as anti-parallelism and the exact base pairings. Unfortunately, history doesn't often give partial marks for discoveries.

Photo 51, the usual piece of evidence cited as proof that her work was stolen, was taken by Franklin's student, Raymond Gosling. If the argument holds that photo 51 being used constitutes "stealing the discovery", then it would be as much his work being stolen as Franklin's. Unfortunately, the reality of scientific research is that lead researchers often take the credit, attention, and funding opportunities that come from major discoveries, that were often enabled by a much larger team of lab assistants, students, post docs, and other researchers.

In the same vein, many of the core elements of Watson and Crick's model had already been proposed by other researchers, such as the structure of each strand of the DNA molecule (proposed by Alexander Todd's research group), and the helical structure (first proposed by Sven Furberg, and then by Franklin's colleague Alexander Stokes). Furberg was also one of the first to suggest a model with the bases on the inside, although he only proposed a single helix. It is never alleged that Crick and Watson stole Furberg's data.

Franklin was an accomplished researcher who published an article in Nature with Gosling, the very same issue as Watson and Crick's paper, and was capable of announcing the discovery had she determined the correct structure. However, Franklin had shifted her focus to the A form of DNA by that point, while photo 51 was of the B form. Another unfortunate reality of invention and scientific discovery is that being first to write your findings down in a format that is acceptable to the broader scientific community is an important step towards getting credit for your work. Alexander Graham Bell, for instance, famously arrived at the patent office mere hours before Elisha Gray, a rival inventor, and is credited with inventing the telephone, even though numerous other inventors, such as Antonio Meucci, likely had working prototypes long before Bell.

unk1.title: Agile has ruined the software industry for all stakeholders. It's time to admit its period of utility is over.

content.paragraph1: Anyone who has worked in the contemporary software development industry has probably worked in an Agile environment, worked with management who implements Scrum or Agile concepts, or at least been exposed to Agile methodologies in some capacity. Agile is like crack for software industry executives; it means that it's always crunch time, features are delivered faster and results are come quicker.
content.paragraph2: For years, the software industry used long term planning when delivering software products. Deliverables and scope were defined at the project outset, deadlines and checkpoints were set (sometimes months or years out), and developers were left to accomplish these tasks. This approach built quality, robust software, but meant the entire development cycle could take years, and the end product could not easily shift to handle changing client expectations or needs.

unk2.title: Dynamic pricing is bad for business.

content.paragraph1: In recent years, we have seen the rise of dynamic pricing, a strategy where businesses adjust the prices of their products or services in real-time based on various factors such as demand, competition, and customer behavior. While businesses may initially find this approach appealing, by allowing them to turn inconsistent consumer demand into a benefit rather than a hindrance, this post will make the case that dynamic pricing will ultimately be a hindrance to consumer businesses, as it erodes consumer trust and the implicit contract between consumers and businesses.
